candidates.name: Get-Process
verified_facts: Get-Process retrieves processes running on the local computer
A process can be selected by process identifier and returned as a System.Diagnostics.Process object
semantic_limits: A live PID alone is insufficient because process identifiers can be reused and command-line identity must also match

candidates.name: Win32_Process
verified_facts: It exposes read-only CommandLine, CreationDate, ExecutablePath, ProcessId and ParentProcessId properties
semantic_limits: Process metadata must match the pinned canonical repo, daemon path, lock record and start time; a matching executable name alone is not ownership proof

candidates.name: Get-Volume
verified_facts: Get-Volume returns volume objects matching specified criteria
Volume output can expose drive letter, health status, size remaining and total size
semantic_limits: Healthy volume status and free space do not prove repository cleanliness, runner ownership or successful Git operations

candidates.name: Get-PSDrive
verified_facts: Get-PSDrive returns drives visible in the current PowerShell session
It includes Windows logical drives and mapped network drives visible to the current user session
semantic_limits: A drive can exist outside the current security context, so missing session visibility must fail closed rather than trigger a destructive remap

candidates.name: Start-Transcript
verified_facts: Start-Transcript creates a text record of all or part of a PowerShell session
The transcript output path can be selected explicitly
semantic_limits: A transcript is audit support only and must not replace structured JSON receipts, hashes or task and attempt identity checks

candidates.name: Stop-Transcript
verified_facts: Stop-Transcript stops a transcript started by Start-Transcript
It returns a status message containing the transcript output path
semantic_limits: Transcript closure does not prove the recorded commands succeeded; exit codes and receipt validation remain required

candidates.name: Get-ExecutionPolicy
verified_facts: Get-ExecutionPolicy returns the effective execution policy for the current session
Get-ExecutionPolicy -List displays policies for each scope in precedence order
semantic_limits: Execution policy is not a security boundary and policy readback does not establish script integrity or successful execution

candidates.name: Get-Command
verified_facts: Get-Command returns commands installed or otherwise available on the system
Command results expose command type, source and version information
semantic_limits: Command discovery does not prove that a command can access the canonical repository, network or required credentials
